classification.difficultyReason: Count multiples in a finite sample space, interpreting simultaneous divisibility as intersections.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

A number is selected at random from the integers 1 to 1000 inclusive. Find the probability the number is:

answer.worked:
There are $1000\div5=200$ multiples of 5.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{divisible by }5)&=\frac{200}{1000}\\P(\text{divisible by }5)&=\frac15\end{align*}$$

$9\times111=999$ and $9\times112=1008$, so there are 111 multiples of 9 in the sample space.

$$P(\text{divisible by }9)=\frac{111}{1000}$$

$11\times90=990$ and $11\times91=1001$, so there are 90 multiples of 11 in the sample space.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{divisible by }11)&=\frac{90}{1000}\\P(\text{divisible by }11)&=\frac9{100}\end{align*}$$

The intersection consists of multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(5,9)=45$. Since $45\times22=990$ and $45\times23=1035$, it contains 22 outcomes.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{divisible by }5\text{ and }9)&=\frac{22}{1000}\\P(\text{divisible by }5\text{ and }9)&=\frac{11}{500}\end{align*}$$

The intersection consists of multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(5,11)=55$. Since $55\times18=990$ and $55\times19=1045$, it contains 18 outcomes.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{divisible by }5\text{ and }11)&=\frac{18}{1000}\\P(\text{divisible by }5\text{ and }11)&=\frac9{500}\end{align*}$$

The intersection consists of multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(9,11)=99$. Since $99\times10=990$ and $99\times11=1089$, it contains 10 outcomes.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{divisible by }9\text{ and }11)&=\frac{10}{1000}\\P(\text{divisible by }9\text{ and }11)&=\frac1{100}\end{align*}$$

The intersection consists of multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(5,9,11)=495$. The only such numbers in the sample space are 495 and 990.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{divisible by }5,9\text{ and }11)&=\frac2{1000}\\P(\text{divisible by }5,9\text{ and }11)&=\frac1{500}\end{align*}$$
